title: Jurisdiction Legal-State Statement (Temporal Model v1)
description: Durable registry record for one legal statement about one jurisdiction, with effective-date semantics. Each record is one state of one (jurisdiction, topic) pair: what the law IS (enacted), what it WILL BE (pending: proposed, passed-but-not-effective, or scheduled-but-conditional), or what it WAS (repealed). Statuses are exactly enacted / pending / repealed in v1; 'pending' subsumes proposed legislation and draft regulation. Honesty anchors: verified_as_of is the date the status was checked against the cited source (a statement may be future-effective and still enacted — enactment is about the legislative state, not the calendar); effective_date is when the statement takes/took effect (null = indeterminate or not pinned by the cited source); retrieved_at is when the source was fetched. review_acknowledged=true marks a stale future-dated statement as reviewed (the validator's stale gate). supersedes_effective_date links a state to the prior state it replaces (Oklahoma-style extensions). See docs/jurisdiction-temporal-model.md for authoring guidance and scripts/audit_jurisdiction_temporal.py for the enforced rules (TEM-01..TEM-10).

jurisdiction_id.description: Canonical jurisdiction profile id (must exist in metadata/id-map.jsonl).

topic.description: The legal dimension the statement covers, e.g. 'adult-use commercial sales', 'home cultivation (adult use)', 'hemp product THC limit'. Free-form but should be stable per topic so successive states and repeals reference the same string.

status.description: enacted = law/regulation is adopted (regardless of whether its effective date has passed); pending = proposed/passed-but-not-yet-law or scheduled-and-conditional (never overwrite current law with this); repealed = in force previously, no longer.

effective_date.description: ISO date the statement takes/took effect, or null when the cited source does not pin one (indeterminate). Required key even when null — absence of a date is data, not an omission.

verified_as_of.description: ISO date the status was verified against source_url. Staleness rules evaluate relative to this date, not to today.

source_url.description: Primary source (regulator, statute, regulation, official dataset) supporting the status. Same evidence rule as the rest of the archive.

retrieved_at.description: ISO date the source was retrieved (mirrors metadata/jurisdiction-sources.jsonl).

review_acknowledged.description: True when a stale future-dated statement (effective date elapsed since verification) has been reviewed and deliberately left unchanged. Silences the validator's stale gate (TEM-05) only; impossibilities still fail.

note.description: Free-text context: conditionality, milestones, scope limits, why a date is null.

supersedes_effective_date.description: effective_date of the prior state of the same topic that this statement replaces. Must be strictly earlier than this record's effective_date.
